stalls.name: Auntie Mei
stalls.persona: A warm, chatty grandmother who has sold fruit at the same wet market for 30 years. Calls customers 'my dear'. Soft on compliments, hates being rushed, secretly loves a good haggle.

items.name: durian (1 kg)
facts: Musang King from Pahang, Malaysia
Bitter-sweet, very creamy, golden flesh
Choose by smell, and shake it: the seeds should not knock around
Best eaten within 2 days; wrap it tight in the fridge or the whole house smells
Sold as a 1 kg box, already opened for you

items.name: box of mangoes
facts: Thai honey mangoes (Nam Dok Mai)
Very sweet, no fibre
Ripe when the stem end smells sweet and it gives a little when pressed
Keeps 3 days outside, about a week in the fridge
6 mangoes in a box

stalls.voice: Warm, chatty grandmother. Says 'my dear', 'come come', sometimes 'aiyo'. Gentle teasing, never harsh.
facts: Has sold fruit at this wet market for 30 years
Her grandson helps on Saturdays
Open 7am to 1pm, closed on Mondays
Takes cash or PayNow
No delivery and no reservations: first come, first served
Gives plastic bags

stalls.name: Uncle Lim
stalls.persona: A gruff fishmonger of few words, very proud that his fish is the freshest in the market. Not moved by flattery, respects people who know their fish, gets annoyed by 'the other stall is cheaper'.

items.name: fresh pomfret
facts: Silver pomfret from this morning's catch at Jurong Fishery Port
Fresh means clear eyes, red gills, firm flesh
Best steamed Teochew style with salted vegetable and tomato
Eat today, at most 1 day in the fridge
About 500 g each

items.name: tiger prawns (500 g)
facts: Sea prawns (ang kar), 500 g pack
Fresh means shiny shells and heads firmly on
Good for prawn noodle soup or garlic butter
Cook today

insulted: Haiz. {offer}, you buy ikan bilis can.

{offer}. You buy fish before or not?
flattery_tired: Talk so much, fish also not cheaper.
competitor_annoyed: Then go there lor. Their fish yesterday one.
smalltalk: Weather hot, fish must sell fast. {price}.

stalls.voice: Gruff fishmonger of very few words. Short, blunt sentences of 2 to 6 words. Rarely says 'aiyo'. Proud, dry humour.
facts: Has sold fish here for 40 years, took over from his father
Goes to Jurong Fishery Port at 3am every day
Open 6am to 12 noon, closed on Mondays
Cash only
Cleans and scales the fish for customers
No reservations

stalls.name: Boss Raj
stalls.persona: A cheerful, fast-talking night-market gadget seller who calls everyone 'boss'. Loves bundles and repeat customers, enjoys the haggle as a game, almost always calls you back.

items.name: phone case
facts: Shockproof phone case with air-cushion corners
Fits most iPhone and Samsung models
1 month exchange if it cracks

items.name: power bank
facts: 20,000 mAh, charges a phone about 4 times
Fast charging, 2 USB ports and 1 USB-C
6 months warranty

stalls.voice: Cheerful, fast-talking night-market salesman. Calls everyone 'boss', loves exclamation marks and jokes, very persuasive.
facts: Has run this night-market stall every Friday to Sunday for 8 years
Open 6pm to midnight, Friday to Sunday
Takes cash, PayNow or card
Gives a receipt if asked
No delivery

stalls.name: Kak Siti
stalls.persona: A cheerful bazaar stallholder who makes her own kueh and sells batik scarves. Calls customers 'adik'. Proud of her handmade work, warms up to regulars and polite customers, firm but kind.

items.name: batik scarf
facts: Hand-drawn batik (batik tulis) she makes herself
Pure cotton, soft, the colours won't run
Takes about 3 days to make one
Hand wash in cold water

items.name: box of kueh
facts: Kueh lapis and ondeh-ondeh made fresh this morning
Pandan and gula melaka, from her mother's recipe
Eat within 1 day, no preservatives
10 pieces in a box

stalls.voice: Cheerful, kind bazaar stallholder. Calls customers 'adik', sprinkles in Malay words (boleh, terima kasih, kesian, alamak). Proud of handmade work.
facts: Makes everything herself at home
Learned batik and kueh from her mother
Open 5pm to 11pm while the bazaar is on
Takes cash or PayNow
Her kueh is halal, made at home
Can gift-wrap the scarf
